text:
The meeting addressed Item 37, a recommendation from Public Works and Parks, Recreation and Marine to award a contract to American Landscape for the Hartwell Park Central Irrigation Renovation Project. The proposed contract amount is capped at $1.6 million and pertains to District Five. The motion to award the contract was made and seconded.

Staff representatives Steve Scott and Craig Beck provided a brief report. Scott explained that the project is part of a long-term initiative to modernize irrigation systems across city parks and medians. He noted that Hartwell Park currently utilizes an older, manual irrigation system, which was a primary reason for prioritizing its replacement. The project has been enhanced with additional funding to support these modernization efforts.

Councilmember Mongo highlighted that the project has undergone significant community outreach and has been in development for approximately four years. He expressed satisfaction at finally moving forward with the system update and urged his colleagues to support the measure. Councilmember Kay Price voiced her support, expressing a hope that similar upgrades would eventually be implemented in all city parks. She acknowledged the high cost of such projects but emphasized the importance of the Hartwell Park renovation due to the park’s high usage rates.

Following the staff report and council comments, the chair called for a vote on the contract award. The discussion focused on the necessity of replacing the outdated manual system with a modernized one to improve operational efficiency in Hartwell Park. No objections to the contract terms or the vendor selection were raised during the recorded segment. The immediate next step is the formal casting of votes by the council members to approve or deny the contract award to American Landscape.
